newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Gains to Slovnaft shares boost SAX index slightly.
newsitem.headline: Gains to Slovnaft shares boost SAX index slightly.

text.p: The Bratislava Stock Exchange, boosted by gains to shares of oil refiner Slovnaft, closed higher on Thursday, as the SAX index rose 2.52 points at 168.74 in thinner trading.

Slovnaft, the most heavily-weighted issue on the bourse, closed up 50 crowns at 780, but brokers said the price did not reflect the share's real value as there were no larger packages available at this level.
Traders said the entire market was still plagued by low liquidity and that small volumes of traded shares prevented prices from reflecting real values of most of the issues.

Libor Briska of Creditanstalt said that investors seemed to be waiting for the result of parliamentary discussions on the controversial securities law, expected within the next two weeks, and that the forthcoming holiday season was also a factor causing sluggish trading activity.
"We don't expect significantly higher activity in the near future, but we think that the index should not resume its downward trend this week," Briska said.
Steel maker VSZ closed up 15 crowns at 485, with 71 shares changing hands, but its average price - used for calculating the index -- eased by 1.4 percent.
VUB lost 10 crowns and closed at 1,670, but traded only 10 shares.
Oil and gas storage company Nafta did not trade today after an extraordinary shareholders meeting on Wednesday failed to dispel investor uncertainty over the company's future.
Overall, volume rose to 254,408 shares, boosted mainly by direct trades, from 249,690 on Wednesday. Turnover increased to 91.72 million crowns from 69.44 million on Wednesday.
